source.anchor: Original Samplinglib supplement: Use a past event on one Itô cell. Exact assumptions and formula below.
source.original_text:
Restrict a progressive integrand to the cell (s,t] and an event known at s. The restricted process is progressive and square integrable. Its completed Itô integral at each fixed time is the original cell increment, truncated at that time, multiplied by the event indicator.

A progressive, real, product-space L² integrand on a positive deterministic horizon T with finite sample measure μ.
One scalar Brownian motion under μ relative to the given filtration. The filtration satisfies the usual conditions.
The deterministic endpoints satisfy 0 ≤ s ≤ t ≤ T.
The event A is measurable in the filtration at time s. The evaluation time u is any fixed time in [0,T].

\begin{gathered}\theta_r(\omega)=\mathbf1_A(\omega)\mathbf1_{\{s<r\le t\}}\eta_r(\omega)\quad\text{for all }r,\omega,\\ I_u(\theta)=\mathbf1_A\bigl(I_{t\wedge u}(\eta)-I_{s\wedge u}(\eta)\bigr)\quad\mu\text{-a.e. for each fixed }u\le T.\end{gathered}

theorem anonymous_target.{u_1}
  {Omega : Type u_1} {m : MeasurableSpace Omega} {filtration : MeasureTheory.Filtration NNReal m}
  {mu : MeasureTheory.Measure Omega} [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure mu] {T : NNReal} {B : NNReal → Omega → ℝ}
  (eta : AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ProgressiveL2.ProgressiveL2Integrand filtration mu T)
  (hT : 0 < T)
  (hB :
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.BrownianMotion.IsBrownianMotionWithFiltration B filtration
      mu)
  (hUsual : AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ProgressiveL2.SatisfiesUsualConditions filtration mu)
  {s t : NNReal} (hst : s ≤ t) (htT : t ≤ T) (event : Set Omega) (hEvent : MeasurableSet event) :
  ∃ theta,
    (∀ (r : NNReal) (omega : Omega),
        theta.process r omega = if omega ∈ event ∧ s < r ∧ r ≤ t then eta.process r omega else 0) ∧
      ∀ u ≤ T,
        AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoIntegralProcess.itoIntegralProcess theta hT hB hUsual
            u =ᵐ[mu]
          fun omega =>
          if omega ∈ event then
            AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoIntegralProcess.itoIntegralProcess eta hT hB
                hUsual (Min.min t u) omega -
              AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoIntegralProcess.itoIntegralProcess eta hT hB
                hUsual (Min.min s u) omega
          else 0

blind_reconstruction.text: Let (Omega,m,mu) be a finite measure space with filtration F, T>0, scalar Brownian motion B with F, and the usual conditions. Here scalar Brownian motion with filtration means centered Gaussian finite-dimensional laws with covariance min(s,t), mu-almost surely continuous paths, strong F-adaptedness, and independence of B(t)-B(s) from F_s for every s<=t. Zero at time zero is part of the scalar law almost surely. Usual conditions mean that every mu-null subset of Omega is in every F_t, and F is right-continuous. A progressive L2 integrand is a real process strongly progressive for F and in L2(mu product lambda_T), where lambda_T is Lebesgue measure restricted to [0,T], transported to NNReal. I_eta denotes its specified continuous completed Ito integral against the given scalar Brownian driver: the canonical limit of elementary integrals, set to zero on its exceptional null set, and held constant after T. Fix a progressive L2 integrand eta on [0,T], deterministic nonnegative times s<=t<=T, and an event E belonging to F_s. There exists a progressive L2 integrand theta on [0,T] such that, pointwise for every r>=0 and omega, theta(r,omega)=1_E(omega)*1_{s<r<=t}*eta(r,omega). Moreover, for every deterministic u<=T, I_theta(u,omega)=1_E(omega)*(I_eta(min(t,u),omega)-I_eta(min(s,u),omega)) for mu-almost every omega. The exceptional set in this last equality may depend on u.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.RandomStoppingProcessConsistency
import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoIntegralProcessCongruence

/-! # A past event as a multiplier on a deterministic Itô cell -/

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoCellMultiplier

open Filter MeasureTheory Set
open scoped NNReal
open BrownianMotion ProgressiveL2 StoppingTime
  ProgressiveL2Algebra ProgressiveL2Stopping ItoIntegralProcess ItoIntegralProcessCongruence
  RandomStoppingProcessConsistency

attribute [local instance] Classical.propDecidable

/-- The literal integrand restricted to a past event and to a right-closed
time cell integrates to the corresponding event times the completed increment. -/
theorem itoIntegralProcess_event_cell_multiplier
    {Omega : Type*} {m : MeasurableSpace Omega}
    {filtration : Filtration ℝ≥0 m} {mu : Measure Omega} [IsFiniteMeasure mu]
    {T : ℝ≥0} {B : ℝ≥0 → Omega → ℝ}
    (eta : ProgressiveL2Integrand filtration mu T) (hT : 0 < T)
    (hB : IsBrownianMotionWithFiltration B filtration mu)
    (hUsual : SatisfiesUsualConditions filtration mu)
    {s t : ℝ≥0} (hst : s ≤ t) (htT : t ≤ T)
    (event : Set Omega) (hEvent : MeasurableSet[filtration s] event) :
    ∃ theta : ProgressiveL2Integrand filtration mu T,
      (∀ (r : ℝ≥0) (omega : Omega),
        theta.process r omega = if omega ∈ event ∧ s < r ∧ r ≤ t then eta.process r omega else 0) ∧
      ∀ u : ℝ≥0, u ≤ T →
        itoIntegralProcess theta hT hB hUsual u =ᵐ[mu]
          fun omega => if omega ∈ event then
            itoIntegralProcess eta hT hB hUsual (min t u) omega -
              itoIntegralProcess eta hT hB hUsual (min s u) omega
            else 0 := by
  classical
  let tau (omega : Omega) := if omega ∈ event then t else s
  have htau : IsChewiStoppingTime filtration (fun omega => (tau omega : WithTop ℝ≥0)) := by
    have hComplement : MeasurableSet[filtration s] eventᶜ :=
      @MeasurableSet.compl Omega event (filtration s) hEvent
    have heq : (fun omega => (tau omega : WithTop ℝ≥0)) =
        eventᶜ.piecewise (fun _ => (s : WithTop ℝ≥0)) (fun _ => (t : WithTop ℝ≥0)) := by
      funext omega
      by_cases he : omega ∈ event <;> simp [tau, Set.piecewise, he] <;> rfl
    rw [heq]
    exact isStoppingTime_piecewise_const hst hComplement
  have htauT (omega : Omega) : tau omega ≤ T := by
    by_cases he : omega ∈ event
    · simpa [tau, he] using htT
    · simpa [tau, he] using hst.trans htT
  let p := stop eta (fun omega => (tau omega : WithTop ℝ≥0)) htau
  let q := stop eta (fun _ => (s : WithTop ℝ≥0)) (isChewiStoppingTime_const filtration s)
  let theta := ProgressiveL2Algebra.sub p q
  refine ⟨theta, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro r omega
    change ((if (r : WithTop ℝ≥0) ≤ (tau omega : WithTop ℝ≥0) then eta.process r omega else 0) -
      (if (r : WithTop ℝ≥0) ≤ (s : WithTop ℝ≥0) then eta.process r omega else 0)) = _
    by_cases he : omega ∈ event
    · rw [show tau omega = t from if_pos he]
      by_cases hrs : r ≤ s
      · rw [if_pos (WithTop.coe_le_coe.mpr (hrs.trans hst)), if_pos (WithTop.coe_le_coe.mpr hrs),
          if_neg (fun h => (not_lt.mpr hrs) h.2.1), sub_self]
      · have hsr : s < r := lt_of_not_ge hrs
        rw [if_neg (fun h => hrs (WithTop.coe_le_coe.mp h)), sub_zero]
        by_cases hrt : r ≤ t
        · rw [if_pos (WithTop.coe_le_coe.mpr hrt), if_pos ⟨he, hsr, hrt⟩]
        · rw [if_neg (fun h => hrt (WithTop.coe_le_coe.mp h)), if_neg (fun h => hrt h.2.2)]
    · rw [show tau omega = s from if_neg he, sub_self, if_neg (fun h => he h.1)]
  · intro u hu
    have heq : (ProgressiveL2Algebra.add theta q).toLp = p.toLp := by
      rw [ProgressiveL2Algebra.toLp_add]
      dsimp only [theta]
      rw [ProgressiveL2Algebra.toLp_sub, sub_add_cancel]
    filter_upwards [itoIntegralProcess_add theta q hT hB hUsual hu,
      itoIntegralProcess_congr_toLp_ae _ _ hT hB hUsual heq hu,
      itoIntegralProcess_stop_ae eta hT tau htau htauT hB hUsual hu,
      itoIntegralProcess_stop_ae eta hT (fun _ => s) (isChewiStoppingTime_const filtration s)
        (fun _ => hst.trans htT) hB hUsual hu] with omega hadd hcon hp hq
    have h := eq_sub_of_add_eq (hadd.symm.trans hcon)
    change itoIntegralProcess theta hT hB hUsual u omega =
      itoIntegralProcess p hT hB hUsual u omega -
        itoIntegralProcess q hT hB hUsual u omega at h
    change itoIntegralProcess p hT hB hUsual u omega =
      itoIntegralProcess eta hT hB hUsual (min (tau omega) u) omega at hp
    change itoIntegralProcess q hT hB hUsual u omega =
      itoIntegralProcess eta hT hB hUsual (min s u) omega at hq
    rw [hp, hq] at h
    by_cases he : omega ∈ event <;> simpa [tau, he] using h

#print axioms itoIntegralProcess_event_cell_multiplier

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoCellMultiplier

steps.title: Switch between two stopping times
steps.text: Take the stop to be t on A and s on its complement. The event and its complement are already known at s, so Mathlib's piecewise constant theorem applies.
steps.lean:
let tau (omega : Omega) := if omega ∈ event then t else s
  have htau : IsChewiStoppingTime filtration (fun omega => (tau omega : WithTop ℝ≥0)) := by
    have hComplement : MeasurableSet[filtration s] eventᶜ :=

        eventᶜ.piecewise (fun _ => (s : WithTop ℝ≥0)) (fun _ => (t : WithTop ℝ≥0)) := by
      funext omega
      by_cases he : omega ∈ event <;> simp [tau, Set.piecewise, he] <;> rfl
    rw [heq]
    exact isStoppingTime_piecewise_const hst hComplement
  have htauT (omega : Omega) : tau omega ≤ T := by
    by_cases he : omega ∈ event
    · simpa [tau, he] using htT
    · simpa [tau, he] using hst.trans htT

steps.title: Subtract the two closed stopped inputs
steps.text: Subtract the input stopped at s from the input stopped at the switch. This yields the exact pointwise event and cell restriction.

steps.title: Use linearity and stopping compatibility
steps.text: The completed integral of the difference equals the difference of the two completed stopped integrals. Evaluate each one at the capped time.
